Let Γ;s be an extended context.
Let t₀, t₁ and t₂ be terms.
If Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁ and Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≤ t₂
then for all extended context Γ′;s′ with Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′,
there exists a term t₃,
such that Γ;s ⊢ t₂ ⟶≡ t₃ and Γ′;s′ ⊢ t₁ ⟶≤ t₃.
Diagrammatically, where the solid arrows are the conditions for the existence of the dashed arrows.
t₂ t₃ t₀ t₁ ≡ ≡ ≤ ≤
Proof.
By induction on the term structure of t₀.
We consider cases according to the last
two rules that are applied respectively in the derivation of the horizontal and
vertical edges of the diagram above, starting by the bottom-left corner.
The cases where bottom rule is rule Me-Top or respectively rule Me-TAp,
then the missing top edge is by rule Me-Top or respectively Me-TAp,
and the missing right edge is by rule Ms-Top.
If the vertical edge rule is Ms-Top,
then the missing top edge is by rule Me-Top,
and the missing right edge is by rule Ms-Top.
If the vertical edge is Ms-Equ, then we have
Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁ and Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₂.
By reflexivity of ⟶≡ (Proposition 18), we have
Γ;s ↣ Γ;s.
Hence by Lemma 2 we have
Γ;s ⊢ t₂ ⟶≡ t₃ and Γ′;s′ ⊢ t₁ ⟶≡ t₃.
Thanks to rule Ms-Equ, from the latter derivation, we obtain Γ′;s′ ⊢ t₁ ⟶≤ t₃.
We know that if the rule Me-Pro appears in the derivation tree Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≤ t₂,
then we have in fact Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₂, and as a result the results follows from
Lemma 2 as outlined by the paragraph outlined above.
We therefore assume that the rule Me-Pro doesn’t appear in the derivation tree Γ;s ⊢ t₀ ⟶≤ t₂,
an information useful only for the last case of this lemma.
Else, for the general case we distinguish the sub-cases below:
Case Me-Pro with Ms-Pro:
We need to prove the diagram below:
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ;s ⊢ x ⟶≡ α′ with x ≡ α∈Γ
Γ;s ⊢ x ⟶≤ t₂ with x ≤ t∈Γ
By prevalidity of the context, we cannot have two distinct annotation for x in the context,
and therefore this case is impossible: there cannot be a subtype annotation and an equivalence
annotation in the prevalid context Γ.
Case Me-Var with Ms-Pro:
We need to prove the diagram below:
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ;s ⊢ x ⟶≡ x.
Γ;s ⊢ x ⟶≤ t by rule Ms-Pro.
From rule Ms-Pro, we know there exists an annotation x ≤ t∈Γ.
Let Γ=Γ₀,x ≤ t,Γ₁ for some context parts Γ₀ and Γ₁.
Let Γ′;s′ be an extended context such that Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
By Lemma 36, we obtain Γ;nil ↣ Γ′;nil
from Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
Now, by multiple use of the rule Ct-Ann
we have Γ′=Γ′₀,x ≤ t′,Γ′₁ with Γ₀;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
By weakening (Lemma 19),
we have Γ₀,x ≤ t,Γ₁;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′ from Γ₀;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
By rule Ms-Pro, we have Γ′;s′ ⊢ x ⟶≤ t′ because x ≤ t′∈Γ′.
The filled diagram is therefore the following: t t′ x x ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
Case Me-App with Ms-App:
We need to prove the diagram below:
u₂ v₀. u₀ v₀ u₁ v₁ ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ;s ⊢ u₀ v₀ ⟶≡ u₁ v₁ by Me-App, which gives us:
Γ;v₀::s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁
Γ;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁
Γ;s ⊢ u₀ v₀ ⟶≤ u₂ v₀ by Ms-App, which gives us:
Γ;v₀::s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≤ u₂
Let Γ′;s′ be an extended context such that Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
By rule Ct-Stk, we have
Γ;v₀::s ↣ Γ′;v₁::s′ from Γ;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁.
By induction hypothesis on u₀, there exists a term u₃ such that:
Γ;v₀::s ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ′;v₁::s′ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
We now have
Γ′;s ⊢ u₂ v₀ ⟶≡ u₃ v₁ by Me-App
from Γ;v₀::s ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃ and Γ;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁
Γ′;s′ ⊢ u₁ v₁ ⟶≤ u₃ v₁ by Ms-App
from Γ′;v₁::s′ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
The filled diagram is therefore the following: u₂ v₀ u₃ v₁ u₀ v₀ u₁ v₁ ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
Case Me-Fun with Ms-Fun:
We need to prove the diagram below:
{λ x ≤ t₀.u₂}. {λ x ≤ t₀.u₀} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₁} ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₀ ⟶≡ λ x ≤ t₁.u₁ by Me-Fun, which gives us:
Γ;nil ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁
Γ,x ≤ t₀;nil ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁
Γ;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₀ ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t₀.u₂ by Ms-Fun, which gives us:
Γ,x ≤ t₀;nil ⊢ u₀ ⟶≤ u₂
Let Γ′;s′ be an extended context such that Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
Because in our case s=nil, we have s′=nil.
By rule Ct-Ann, we have Γ,x ≤ t₀;nil ↣ Γ′,x ≤ t₁;nil
from Γ;nil ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁.
By induction hypothesis on u₀, there exists a term u₃ such that:
Γ,x ≤ t₀;nil ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ′,x ≤ t₁;nil ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
We now have
Γ;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₂ ⟶≡ λ x ≤ t₁.u₃ by Me-Fun
from Γ;nil ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁ and Γ,x ≤ t₀;nil ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ′;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t₁.u₁ ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t₁.u₃ by Ms-Fun
from Γ′,x ≤ t₁;nil ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
The filled diagram is therefore the following: {λ x ≤ t₀.u₂} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₃} {λ x ≤ t₀.u₀} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₁} ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
Case Me-FOp with Ms-FOp:
We need to prove the diagram below:
{λ x ≤ t₀.u₂}. {λ x ≤ t₀.u₀} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₁} ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ;α::s ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₀ ⟶≡ λ x ≤ t₁.u₁ by Me-FOp, which gives us:
Γ;nil ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁
Γ,x ≡ α;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁
Γ;α::s ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₀ ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t₀.u₂ by Ms-FOp, which gives us:
Γ,x ≡ α;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≤ u₂
Let Γ′;s′ be an extended context such that Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
In our case, we have s=α::s₀ and s′=α′::s₁ with by rule Ct-Stk, Γ;nil ⊢ α ⟶≡ α′.
By rule Ct-Stk, we have Γ;s₀ ↣ Γ′;s₁
and Γ;nil ⊢ α ⟶≡ α′
from Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
We now have Γ,x ≡ α;s₀ ↣ Γ′,x ≡ α′;s₁ by rule Ct-Ann.
By induction hypothesis on u₀, there exists a term u₃ such that:
Γ,x ≡ α;s₀ ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ′,x ≡ α′;s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
We now have
Γ;α::s₀ ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₂ ⟶≡ λ x ≤ t₁.u₃ by Me-FOp
from Γ;nil ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁ and Γ,x ≡ α;s₀ ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ′;α′::s₁ ⊢ λ x ≤ t₁.u₁ ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t₁.u₃ by Ms-FOp
from Γ′,x ≡ α′;s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
The filled diagram is therefore the following: {λ x ≤ t₀.u₂} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₃} {λ x ≤ t₀.u₀} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₁} ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
Case Me-Bet with Ms-App:
We need to prove the diagram below:
{(λ x ≤ t.u₂) v₀}. {(λ x ≤ t.u₀) v₀} u₁[x v₁] ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ;s ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u₀) v₀ ⟶≡ u₁[x v₁] by Me-Bet, which gives us:
Γ;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁
Γ;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁
Γ;s ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u₀) ⟶≤ (λ x ≤ t.u₂) v₀ by Ms-App, which gives us:
Γ;v₀::s ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u₀ ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t.u₂
By Ms-FOp, this implies Γ,x ≡ v₀;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≤ u₂
Let Γ′;s′ be an extended context such that Γ;s ↣ Γ′;s′.
As explained in the introduction paragraph of this lemma,
we know that in the derivation tree of Γ,x ≡ v₀;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≤ u₂
then the rule Me-Pro isn’t used
(which is because otherwise we’d have Γ,x ≡ v₀;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂
and we conclude by Lemma 2).
Therefore this derivation is in fact Γ;s ⊢ u₀ ⟶≤ u₂.
By induction hypothesis on u₀, there exists a term u₃ such that:
Γ;s ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ′;s′ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃
It is important to note that x is a fresh variable created by the lambdas of this case,
and therefore by alpha conversion there is no instance of x in s, hence s[x v₁]=s.
By a similar reasoning, we know that there is no x isn’t in the domain of Γ′.
As a result, the derivation Γ′;s′ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₃ do not make a promotion of x.
Hence by Lemma 30, we obtain
Γ′;s′ ⊢ u₁[x v₁]⟶≤ u₃[x v₁].
By rule Me-Bet, we obtain
Γ;s ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u₂) v₀ ⟶≡ u₃[x v₁] from
Γ;s ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃ and Γ;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁.
The filled diagram is therefore the following: {(λ x ≤ t.u₂) v₀} u₃[x v₁] {(λ x ≤ t.u₀) v₀} u₁[x v₁] ≡ ≤ ≡ ≤

Let Γ₀;s₀ be an extended context.
Let t₀, t₁, and t₂ be terms.
If Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₂,
then for any extended contexts
Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₂;s₂ such that Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂,
there exists a term t₃
such that Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ t₁ ⟶≡ t₃ and Γ₂;s₂ ⊢ t₂ ⟶≡ t₃.
Moreover, for any variable x, if in the derivation of Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁
(respectively Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₂ )
there isn’t an application of the Rule Me-Pro that makes a promotion of variable x,
then in the derivation Γ₂;s₂ ⊢ t₂ ⟶≡ t₃
(respectively Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ t₁ ⟶≡ t₃ )
there won’t be an application of the Rule Me-Pro that makes a promotion of variable x.
Diagrammatically, the existence of the solid arrows implies the existence of the dashed arrows: t₂ t₃ t₀ t₁ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
Proof.
We now proceed by induction on the derivation tree of Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁.
We consider cases according to the last
two rules that are applied respectively in the derivation of the horizontal and
vertical edges of the diagram above, starting by the bottom-left corner. The base case
corresponds to when these two rules are both Me-Top (respectively both Me-Var),
for which the lemma holds by using the rule Me-Top (respectively Me-Var) for the missing edges.
For the general case we distinguish the subcases below:
Case Me-Pro and Me-Var:
We need to prove the diagram below: α₁. x x ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ x ⟶≡ x.
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ x ⟶≡ α₁ with x ≡ α₀∈Γ₀ and Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₁.
Let Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₂;s₂ be extended contexts such that
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂.
By Lemma 36,
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂ implies
Γ₀;nil ↣ Γ₂;nil.
Because Γ₀ is of the form Γ₀′,x ≡ α₀,Γ₀″,
we have Γ₂=Γ₂′,x ≡ α₂,Γ₂″.
By multiple use of the rule Ct-Ann, we have Γ₀′;nil ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₂.
By weakening (Lemma 19), we have Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₂.
By induction hypothesis on Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₁, there exists a term α₃ such that:
Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ α₁ ⟶≡ α₃
Γ₂;s₂ ⊢ α₂ ⟶≡ α₃
By rule Me-Pro, we have Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ x ⟶≡ α₃ from
x ≡ α₁∈Γ₁ and Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ α₁ ⟶≡ α₃.
The filled diagram is therefore the following: α₁ α₃ x x ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
Case Me-Pro and Me-Pro:
We need to prove the diagram below: α₂. x α₁ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₁ with x ≡ α₀∈Γ₀ and Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₁.
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₂ with x ≡ α₀∈Γ₀ and Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₂.
Let Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₂;s₂ be extended contexts such that
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂.
By induction hypothesis on Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ α₀ ⟶≡ α₁, there exists a term α₃ such that:
Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ α₁ ⟶≡ α₃
Γ₂;s₂ ⊢ α₂ ⟶≡ α₃
The filled diagram is therefore the following: α₂ α₃ x α₁ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
Case Me-App and Me-App:
We need to prove the diagram below: u₂ v₂. u₀ v₀ u₁ v₁ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ v₀ ⟶≡ u₁ v₁ by rule Me-App, which gives us:
Γ₀;v₀::s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁
Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ v₀ ⟶≡ u₂ v₂ by rule Me-App, which gives us:
Γ₀;v₀::s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂
Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₂
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂
Let Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₂;s₂ be extended contexts such that
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂.
By rule Ct-Stk, we know:
Γ₀;v₀::s₀ ↣ Γ₁;v₁::s₁ from Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁
Γ₀;v₀::s₀ ↣ Γ₂;v₂::s₂ from Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₂
By induction hypothesis on Γ₀;v₀::s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁, there exists a term u₃ such that:
Γ₁;v₁::s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ₂;v₂::s₂ ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
By Lemma 36, respectively Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂
implies respectively
Γ₀;nil ↣ Γ₁;nil and Γ₀;nil ↣ Γ₂;nil.
By induction hypothesis on Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁, there exists a term v₃ such that:
Γ₁;nil ⊢ v₁ ⟶≡ v₃
Γ₂;nil ⊢ v₂ ⟶≡ v₃
We now have:
Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ u₁ v₁ ⟶≡ u₃ v₃ by rule Me-App
from Γ₁;v₁::s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₃ and Γ₁;nil ⊢ v₁ ⟶≡ v₃
Γ₂;s₂ ⊢ u₂ v₂ ⟶≡ u₃ v₃ by rule Me-App
from Γ₂;v₂::s₂ ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃ and Γ₂;nil ⊢ v₂ ⟶≡ v₃
The filled diagram is therefore the following: u₂ v₂ u₃ v₃ u₀ v₀ u₁ v₁ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
Case Me-App with Me-Bet:
We need to prove the diagram below: u₂[x v₂]. {(λ x ≤ t₀.u₀)v₀} {(λ x ≤ t₁.u₁)v₁} ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ (λ x ≤ t₀.u₀)v₀ ⟶≡ (λ x ≤ t₁.u₁)v₁ by rule Me-App, which gives us:
Γ₀;v₀::s₀ ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₀ ⟶≡ λ x ≤ t₁.u₁.
By rule Me-FOp, this implies Γ₀;nil ⊢ t₀ ⟶≡ t₁ and Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₁
Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ (λ x ≤ t₀.u₀)v₀ ⟶≡ u₂[x v₂] by rule Me-Bet, which gives us:
Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂
Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₂
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂
Let Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₂;s₂ be extended contexts such that
Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂.
By weakening (Lemma 19), we obtain Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂
from Γ₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂,
and we also know that the derivation Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂ do not make a promotion of x to v₀.
We have by rule Ct-Ann,
Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁,x ≡ v₁;s₁ from Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁.
Similarly we have Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂,x ≡ v₂;s₂.
By induction hypothesis on Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂, there exists a term u₃ such that:
Γ₁,x ≡ v₁;s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₃
Γ₂,x ≡ v₂;s₂ ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃
Because the derivation Γ₀,x ≡ v₀;s₀ ⊢ u₀ ⟶≡ u₂ do not make any promotion of x to v₀,
then the induction process ensures that the derivation Γ₁,x ≡ v₁;s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₃
do not make any promotion of x to v₁.
As a result we have Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₃.
By Lemma 36, respectively Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₁;s₁ and Γ₀;s₀ ↣ Γ₂;s₂
implies respectively
Γ₀;nil ↣ Γ₁;nil and Γ₀;nil ↣ Γ₂;nil.
By induction hypothesis on Γ₀;nil ⊢ v₀ ⟶≡ v₁, there exists a term v₃ such that:
Γ₁;nil ⊢ v₁ ⟶≡ v₃
Γ₂;nil ⊢ v₂ ⟶≡ v₃
We now have:
Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ (λ x ≤ t₁.u₁)v₁ ⟶≡ u₃[x v₃] by rule Me-Bet
from Γ₁;s₁ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₃ and Γ₁;nil ⊢ v₁ ⟶≡ v₃
Γ₂;s₂ ⊢ u₂[x v₂]⟶≡ u₃[x v₃] by Lemma 32
from Γ₂,x ≡ v₂;s₂ ⊢ u₂ ⟶≡ u₃ and Γ₂;nil ⊢ v₂ ⟶≡ v₃
The filled diagram is therefore the following: u₂[x v₂] u₃[x v₃] {(λ x ≤ t₀.u₀)v₀} {(λ x ≤ t₁.u₁)v₁} ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
Case Me-App with Me-TAp:
We need to prove the diagram below: ⊤ ⊤ ⊤ u ⊤ u′ ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
The top edge holds by rule Me-Top.
The right edge holds by rule Me-TAp.
Case Me-Fun with Me-Fun:
We need to prove the diagram below: {λ x ≤ t₂.u₂}. {λ x ≤ t₀.u₀} {λ x ≤ t₁.u₁} ≡ ≡ ≡ ≡
By assumption, we have the following reductions:
Γ₀;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t₀.u₀ ⟶≡ λ x ≤ t₁.u₁ by rule Me-Fun, which gives us:

paper: Theorem 4 (Progress).
Let t be a term. For every logical context Γ, if Γ ⊢ t wf then either t is
in normal form, or there exists a term t′ such that t ↦ t′.
Proof.
By structural induction on the term t. If t is ⊤ or a variable x, then the result holds
since t is already in normal form. Therefore it suffices to consider the following cases:
Case t=λ x ≤ u.v with u∉NF :
By assumption we have
Γ ⊢ λ x ≤ u.v wf. By rule Wf-Fun,
we obtain Γ ⊢ u wf. By the induction hypothesis
on u, there exists u′ such that u ↦ u′, and as a result
t ↦ λ x ≤ u′.v by rule Os-Con.
Case t=λ x ≤ u_n.v with v∉NF :
By assumption we have
Γ ⊢ λ x ≤ u_n.v wf. By rule Wf-Fun,
we have that Γ,x ≤ u_n ⊢ v wf.
By using the induction hypothesis on v, there exists v′
such that v ↦ v′, and as a result t ↦ λ x ≤ u_n.v′ by rule
Os-Con.
Case t=u v with u∉NF :
By assumption we have
Γ ⊢ u v wf. By rule Wf-App and Proposition 12 we have
Γ ⊢ u wf. Since u is not a normal form and by the induction
hypothesis, there exists a term u′ such that u ↦ u′, and therefore
t ↦ u′ v by rule Os-Con.
Case t=u_n v with v∉NF.
By assumption we have
Γ ⊢ u_n v wf.
By rule Wf-App and Proposition 12 we have
Γ ⊢ v wf. Since v is not a normal form and by the induction
hypothesis, there exists a term v′ such that v ↦ v′, and therefore
t ↦ u_n v′ by rule Os-Con.
Case t=u_n v_n with u_n∈NF and v_n∈NF.
Term u_n is either ⊤, a
function, or a neutral applied to multiple normal forms. If u_n is a function, then t is a redex can be reduced by
rule Os-Bet.
The case where u_n is ⊤ is impossible, indeed
from the fact that t is well-formed, by rule W-App we have u_n a subtype of a function λ x ≤ t′.⊤.
If u_n is ⊤, it cannot have a function supertype by Lemma 11.
Else, if u_n is a neutral applied to multiple normal forms,
then t=u_n v_n, because v_n is in normal form, is also a neutral applied to multiple normal forms,
and therefore t is in normal form. ∎

4.account: Induction on local closure, reading the well-formedness derivation alongside. The application case is the only one that consults the derivation, and Theorem 11 is what excludes a stuck ⊤ in operator position. Reuses v1's context-free normal-form and ↦ machinery.

paper: Theorem 5 (Preservation).
Let Γ be a logical context.
Let t, t′, and u be terms. If
Γ ⊢ t ≤*wf u and t ↦ t′, then
Γ ⊢ t′ ≤*wf u.
Proof.
To prove Γ ⊢ t′ ≤*wf u we use rule Ws-Trs
and prove Γ ⊢ t′ ≤*wf t and Γ ⊢ t ≤*wf u.
We already have Γ ⊢ t ≤*wf u, so we only prove Γ ⊢ t′ ≤*wf t.
From the assumption Γ ⊢ t ≤*wf u and by
Proposition 12 we know that
Γ ⊢ t wf. We obtain Γ ⊢ t′ wf from the Γ ⊢ t wf established
earlier and by Lemma 6 and t ↦ t′.
By rule Ws-Rfl and Ws-Sub, we have
Γ ⊢ t′ ≤*wf t′,
hence Γ ⊢ t′ ≤*wf t by rule Ws-Rgh.

paper: Lemma 7 (Substitution preserves well-formedness).
Let Γ and Γ′ be logical contexts, and let t, u and α be terms.
Let x be a variable.
If
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u wf, and
Γ ⊢ α≤*wf t,
then
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u[x\α] wf.
Proof.
First, we establish that Γ,Γ′[x\α] is prevalid by
Lemma 28, which we’ll use in most of the cases
below. Now we proceed by induction on the derivation tree of
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u wf. We distinguish cases on the last rule used:
Rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE, with u=y and y ◁ t′∈Γ :
By assumption, we have y ◁ t′∈Γ hence
y ◁ t′∈Γ∪Γ′[x\α].
As proven at the start of this lemma, we have Γ,Γ′[x\α] prevalid,
hence Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ y wf by rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE.
Rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE, with u=y and y ◁ t′∈Γ′ :
From the fact that y ◁ t′ is a subtype annotation of Γ′, we have that
y ◁ t′[x\α] is a subtype annotation of Γ′[x\α] by
definition of the substitution of extended context which doesn’t change the domain of the logical context.
We also have y ◁ t′[x\α]∈Γ∪Γ′[x\α]
from y ◁ t′[x\α]∈Γ′[x\α].
As proven at the start of this lemma, we have Γ,Γ′[x\α] prevalid,
we can now conclude that
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ y wf by rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE.
Rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE, with u=x :
By assumption of our lemma, we have Γ ⊢ α wf,
hence by weakening (Lemma 19), Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ α wf,
which is the desired result of this case.
Rule Wf-Top, with u=⊤ :
We have
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ ⊤ wf since
Γ,Γ′[x\α] is prevalid and by rule Wf-Top.
Rule Wf-Fun, with u=λ y ≤ v.u′ :
Without loss of generality we can assume that y≠x because we can always alpha convert the variable y to a different name.
By assumption and by the rule used, we
have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ v wf and
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,y ≤ v ⊢ u′ wf. By the induction hypothesis, we obtain
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ v[x\α] wf and
Γ,Γ′[x\α],y ≤ v[x\α]⊢ u′[x\α] wf.
Now, we obtain
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ λ y ≤ v[x\α].u′[x\α] wf by rule Wf-Fun,
which equals Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ (λ y ≤ v.u′)[x\α] wf
since y≠x by definition of the substitution.
Rule Wf-App with u=v u′ :
By Wf-App on our assumption, we have
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf z and
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ v ≤*wf λ y ≤ z.⊤.
Let’s prove by induction on
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf z
that we have
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u′[x\α]≤*wf z[x\α].
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf z.
Rule Ws-Sub:
In this case our derivation is Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf z
with premises Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ ≤wf z, Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ wf
and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ z wf.
In that case, by the result we will prove below, we have
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u′[x\α]≤*wf z[x\α].
Rule Ws-Trs:
In this case our derivation is Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf z

paper: Lemma 9.
Let Γ;s be an extended context, and Γ′ be a logical context,
such that Γ,Γ′[x\α];nil is prevalid.
Let u, v, t and α be terms, such that
both u[x\α] and v[x\α] are well-formed in context Γ,Γ′[x\α].
If Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v,
and Γ ⊢ α≤*wf t.
Then Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]≤*wf v[x\α].
Proof.
In this lemma, we have two cases, either the derivation Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v
depending on if our derivation is of the form Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[x]⟶≤ Co[t] for some covariant context Co.
If it is:
By assumption, we have both u[x\α] and v[x\α] well-formed in context Γ,Γ′[x\α],
because the derivation Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v
is Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[x]⟶≤ Co[t],
these terms are Co_[x\α][α] and Co_[x\α][t].
From Γ ⊢ α≤*wf t we have by weakening (Lemma 19)
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α]⊢ α≤*wf t.
We therefore have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α]⊢ α≤*wf t,
and both Co_[x\α][α] and Co_[x\α][t] well-formed in Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α].
Hence by Conjecture 8, we obtain
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α]⊢ Co_[x\α][α]≤*wf Co_[x\α][t].
Because there is no instance of the variable x in neither α nor in t,
this last derivation is
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]≤*wf v[x\α].
By prevalidity of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α], we know that there is no instance of the variable x
in Γ. As a result, there is no instance of this variable anywhere.
As a result, we have
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]≤*wf v[x\α] the desired result.
Else:
We apply Lemma 30 to obtain
Γ,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ u[x\α]⟶≤ v[x\α].
By rule Ws-Rfl, we have
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ v[x\α]≤wf v[x\α].
Hence, by rule Ws-Lft,
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]≤wf v[x\α].
Because both terms are well-formed by assumption, we have by rule Ws-Sub,
Γ,Γ′[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]≤*wf v[x\α]
the desired result.

paper: Lemma 10 (Inversion lemma.).
Let Γ be a logical context.
Let λ x ≤ t.u and λ x ≤ t′.u′ be terms.
If Γ ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u) ≤*wf (λ x ≤ t′.u′) then
Γ ⊢ t ≡wf t′.
Proof.
By induction on the number of transitivity step of
Γ ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u) ≤*wf (λ x ≤ t′.u′),
we obtain Γ ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u) ≤* (λ x ≤ t′.u′)
by applying Proposition 13 on each of these transitivity steps.
By transitivity elimination (Lemma 3), we then obtain
Γ;nil ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u) ≤ (λ x ≤ t′.u′).
By definition, there exists a term z such that
Γ;nil ⊢ (λ x ≤ t.u) ⟶≡↠ z and
Γ;nil ⊢ (λ x ≤ t′.u′) ⟶≤↠ z.
On the first derivation, based on the structure of the term λ x ≤ t.u,
only the rule Me-Fun can be applied, and therefore there exists a function
λ x ≤ t_z.u_z such that z=λ x ≤ t_z.u_z.
Because only the rule Me-Fun has been applied, we also have
Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ t_z.
We apply the same reasoning on the derivation Γ;nil ⊢ (λ x ≤ t′.u′) ⟶≤↠ z,
which consists only of use of the rule Ms-Fun or Ms-Equ with Me-Fun,
and therefore we have as well Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ t_z.
By rule Ws-Rfl, we have Γ ⊢ t_z ≡wf t_z.
We now show that we have Γ ⊢ t ≡wf t_z by induction on the number of derivation steps of
Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ t_z. If there is no derivation step, then we have t=t_z and the result holds.
Otherwise, there exists a term t′ such that Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′
and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ t_z. By the induction hypothesis on the number of derivation steps of
Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ t_z, we obtain Γ ⊢ t′ ≡wf t_z.
By rule Ws-Lf1 on Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′ and Γ ⊢ t′ ≡wf t_z,
we obtain Γ ⊢ t ≡wf t_z.
By the same reasoning on the number of derivation steps of Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ t_z,
we obtain Γ ⊢ t ≡ t′ from Γ ⊢ t ≡wf t_z and the rule Ws-Rgh.

paper: Theorem 11 (No supertype of Top.).
Let Γ;s be an extended context.
Let λ x ≤ t.u be a term. We cannot
have Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ≤* λ x ≤ t.u.
Proof.
First we transform Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ≤* λ x ≤ t.u
into Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ≤ λ x ≤ t.u by transitivity elimination (Lemma 3).
Assume towards a contradiction that
Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ≤ λ x ≤ t.u. By definition of the subtyping relation, there exists w
such that Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ⟶≤↠ w and Γ;s ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ⟶≡↠ w.
From Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ⟶≤↠ w, we obtain that w=⊤
since ⊤ can only promote to itself, with rules Ms-Equ and
Ms-Top. Now from Γ;s ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ⟶≡↠ w, we know that w is an
abstraction since the only rule for equivalence reduction that can be applied to
λ x ≤ t.u is rule Ms-Fun or Ms-FOp. But this contradicts the w=⊤ established
earlier and we are done.

paper: Proposition 12 (Well-formedness extraction).
Let Γ be an extended context and u and v be terms. If
Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v then both derivation Γ ⊢ u wf and
Γ ⊢ v wf exist in the derivation tree Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v.
Proof.
Note: the requirement that the derivation trees ( Γ ⊢ u wf and Γ ⊢ v wf )
exist in the original derivation tree is used on other lemmas because we do induction on derivation trees.
It is not enough to know that Γ ⊢ u wf and Γ ⊢ v wf exist,
they need to be a subtree of our original tree. Hence this formulation.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v. If the last
rule applied is Ws-Sub, then the result holds from the assumption of the rule.
Else, the last rule applied is Wf-Trans, then there exists a term t such that
Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf t and Γ ⊢ t ≤*wf v, and the result
holds by the induction hypothesis.
12.sig: Prop-12 : ∀ {Γ u m t} → Γ ⊢ u ⊑*wf[ m ] t → (Γ ⊢ u wf) × (Γ ⊢ t wf)
12.account: Direct induction on the well-subtyping derivation, reading the well-formedness off Ws-Sub's premises.

paper: Proposition 13 (From well-subtyping to subtyping.).
Let Γ be a logical context and u and v be terms. If
Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v then Γ;nil ⊢ u ≤ v.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree.
Rule Ws-Rfl:
In this case, we have u=v=t.
By Proposition 18, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t.
By rule Ms-Equ, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≤ t.
By definition of the subtype relation ≤, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ≤ t.
Rule Ws-Lf1 or Ws-Lf2:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ v′ ≤wf t,
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ;nil ⊢ v′ ≤ t.
By definition of ≤, there exists z such that Γ;nil ⊢ v′ ⟶≤↠ z and Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ z.
The reduction Γ;nil ⊢ v{{◁}{}}v′ is
either Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′ or Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′.
In the former case, by rule Ms-Equ, we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′.
Hence we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′.
Hence Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤↠ v′.
We now have Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤↠ v′ and Γ;nil ⊢ v′ ⟶≤↠ z, hence Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤↠ z.
By definition of ≤, we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ≤ t.
Rule Ws-Rgh:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ v ≤wf t′,
Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ;nil ⊢ v ≤ t′.
By definition of ≤, there exists z such that Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤↠ z and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ z.
By definition of ⟶≡, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≤ t′ and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≤ t.
Hence Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≤↠ t′.
We now have Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ z, hence Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≤↠ z and Γ;nil ⊢ z ⟶≤↠ t′.
We have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≤↠ t′ and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≤↠ z, hence Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≤↠ z.
By definition of ≤, we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ≤ t.
13.sig: ⊑wf⇒⊲ : ∀ {Γ u m t} → Γ ⊢ u ⊑wf[ m ] t → Γ ∣ [] ⊢ u ⊲[ m ] t
13.account: Direct induction. Worth noting the shift the modes force: Ws-Lf1 takes an equivalence step where As-Left-1 demands a promotion, so the subtyping reading routes through Ms-Equ.

paper: Proposition 14 (From well-equivalence to equivalence.).
Let Γ be a logical context and u and v be terms. If
Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v then Γ;nil ⊢ u ≡ v.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree.
Rule Ws-Rfl:
In this case, we have u=v=t.
By Proposition 18, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t.
By rule Ms-Equ, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t.
By definition of the subtype relation ≡, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ≡ t.
Rule Ws-Lf1:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ v′ ≡wf t,
Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ;nil ⊢ v′ ≡ t.
By definition of ≡, there exists z such that Γ;nil ⊢ v′ ⟶≡↠ z and Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ z.
From Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′ we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ v′.
We now have Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ v′ and Γ;nil ⊢ v′ ⟶≡↠ z, hence Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ z.
By definition of ≡, we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ≡ t.
Rule Ws-Rgh:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ v ≡wf t′,
Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ;nil ⊢ v ≡ t′.
By definition of ≡, there exists z such that Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ z and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ z.
By definition of ⟶≡, we have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′ and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡ t.
Hence Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ t′.
We now have Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ z, hence Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ z and Γ;nil ⊢ z ⟶≡↠ t′.
We have Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ t′ and Γ;nil ⊢ t′ ⟶≡↠ z, hence Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡↠ z.
By definition of ≡, we have Γ;nil ⊢ v ≡ t.
14.sig: Prop-14 : ∀ {Γ u t} → Γ ⊢ u ≋wf t → Γ ∣ [] ⊢ u ≋ t
14.account: The equivalence-mode counterpart of Proposition 13, by the same induction.

paper: Lemma 15.
Let Γ be a logical context and u and v be terms. If
Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v then Γ ⊢ v ≡wf u.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree.
Rule Ws-Rfl:
In this case, we have u=v.
By rule Ws-Rfl, we have Γ ⊢ u ≡wf u.
Rule Ws-Lf1:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ u′ ≡wf v,
Γ;nil ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ ⊢ v ≡wf u′.
By rule Ws-Rgh, we obtain Γ ⊢ v ≡wf u.
Rule Ws-Rgh:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v′,
Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ ⊢ v′ ≡wf u.
By rule Ws-Lf1, we obtain Γ ⊢ v ≡wf u.
15.sig: Lem-15 : ∀ {Γ u t} → Γ ⊢ u ≋wf t → Γ ⊢ t ≋wf u

paper: Lemma 16.
Let Γ be a logical context and u and v be terms. If
Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v then Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree.
Rule Ws-Rfl:
In this case, we have u=v.
By rule Ws-Rfl, we have Γ ⊢ u ≤wf u.
Rule Ws-Lf1:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ u′ ≡wf v,
Γ;nil ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ ⊢ u′ ≤wf v.
Hence by rule Ws-Lf1, we obtain Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v.
Rule Ws-Rgh:
In this case, we have as premises Γ ⊢ u ≡wf v′,
Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′.
By induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v′.
Hence by rule Ws-Rgh, we obtain Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v.
16.sig: Lem-16 : ∀ {Γ u t} → Γ ⊢ u ≋wf t → Γ ⊢ u ≤wf t
16.account: Induction on ⊑wf[eqv-m], keeping each rule and changing only the mode index.

paper: Proposition 17 (From reduction semantics to equivalence reduction.).
Let u and v be terms.
If u ↦ v then Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v for all extended context Γ;s.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of u ↦ v. The base case is when the last
rule used is Os-Bet, and the result holds by rule Me-Bet and
reflexivity of ⟶≡ (Proposition 18).
The induction cases is when the last rule used is Os-Con, and the result holds
by induction and rules Me-Fun, Me-FOp and Me-App.

Exhaustive case analysis on the derivation: Me-App cannot produce a variable in operator position, and Me-Bet's body premise is stuck.

paper: Proposition 18 (Reflexivity.).
Let Γ;s be an extended context, and u be a term,
we have Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ u, and Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ u.

Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ u, noting that the
only applicable rules at the leaves are Me-Top and Me-Var,
and that at the rest of the nodes only rules
Me-App, Me-Fun, and Me-FOp occur.
To now prove Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ u, we use rule Ms-Equ.

paper: Lemma 19 (Weakening of context).
Let Γ;s and Γ′;s′ be two extended contexts such that Γ,Γ′;s@s′ is prevalid.
Let u and v be terms.
We have the following relations:
If Γ ⊢ u wf then Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u wf.
If Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v then Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤wf v.
If Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v then Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤*wf v.
If Γ;s ⊢ u ≤ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤ v.
If Γ;s ⊢ u ≤* v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤* v.
If Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
If Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ v.
If Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v then Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
If Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ v then Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ v.
Proof.
Note: this lemma is a group of different lemmas which are proved separately.
This proof dispatches the proof of each of these lemmas to their respective proof.
We do a case disjunction based on the case we are in:
Case Γ ⊢ u wf or Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v or Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v :
Done in Lemma 20.
Case Γ;s ⊢ u ≤ v :
We need to prove that if Γ;s ⊢ u ≤ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤ v.
By definition of the relation ≤, there exists a term z such that
Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ z and Γ;s ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ z.
By using respectively Lemma 21 and Lemma 22
on respectively Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ z and Γ;s ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ z,
we respectively obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ z and Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ v ⟶≡↠ z.
By definition of the relation ≤, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤ v.
Case Γ;s ⊢ u ≤* v :
We need to prove that if Γ;s ⊢ u ≤* v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤* v.
By definition of the relation ≤*,
there exists u₁,,u_n such that
Γ;s ⊢ u ≤ u₁, Γ;s ⊢ u₁ ≤ u₂,·s,Γ;s ⊢ u_n ≤ v.
By using the reasoning of the case above on each Γ;s ⊢ u_i ≤ u_i+1, we obtain
Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤ u₁, Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u₁ ≤ u₂,·s,Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u_n ≤ v.
By definition of the relation ≤*, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ≤* v.
Case Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v :
We need to prove that if Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
We proceed by induction on the derivation tree of Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
The proof can be found in Lemma 21.
Case Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ v :
We need to prove that if Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ v.
By definition of the relation ⟶≤↠, there exists u₁,,u_n such that
Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ u₁, Γ;s ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₂,·s,Γ;s ⊢ u_n ⟶≤ v.
By using Lemma 21 multiple times, we obtain
Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ u₁, Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u₁ ⟶≤ u₂,·s,Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u_n ⟶≤ v.
By definition of the relation ⟶≤↠, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ v.
Case Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v :
We need to prove that if Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v then Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
We proceed by induction on the derivation tree of Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
The proof can be found in Lemma 22.
Case Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ v :
We need to prove that if Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ v then Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ v.
By definition of the relation ⟶≡↠, there exists u₁,,u_n such that
Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ u₁, Γ;s ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₂,·s,Γ;s ⊢ u_n ⟶≡ v.
By using Lemma 22 multiple times, we obtain
Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡ u₁, Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u₁ ⟶≡ u₂,·s,Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u_n ⟶≡ v.
By definition of the relation ⟶≡↠, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ v.

paper: Lemma 20 (Weakening of context - Aux).
Let Γ and Γ′ be two logical contexts such that Γ,Γ′ is prevalid.
Let u and v be terms.
We have the following relations:
If Γ ⊢ u wf then Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u wf.
If Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v then Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤wf v.
If Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v then Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤*wf v.
Proof.
We need to prove all of these relations together, because any derivation tree of any of these relations
will contain a derivation tree of the other relations.
Consider for instance Γ ⊢ (λ x ≤ ⊤.x) ⊤ wf.
One of the premise of this derivation tree is Γ ⊢ ⊤ ≤*wf ⊤,
which will ultimately have as premise Γ ⊢ ⊤ ≤wf ⊤ and Γ ⊢ ⊤ wf.
The proof therefore consider all of these relations together.
The proof works by induction on the derivation tree,
for the example above for instance, Γ ⊢ ⊤ wf is considered a base case, and therefore
we have Γ,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ wf, from which we will be able to conclude Γ,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ ≤wf ⊤,
and so on.
Assume any of the cases of this lemma.
We do an induction on the size of the derivation tree of either
(Γ ⊢ u wf)₁, (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂ or (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃
which we index by i for i∈\1,2,3\ as a indexed family,
one of the three possible cases of this lemma.
The induction hypothesis can be called on any element of this family, as long as the size of its derivation tree
is smaller.
For instance, consider a derivation tree ending by the rule Wf-App
(for instance (Γ ⊢ u v wf)₁ ), its premises are
derivations of the form (Γ ⊢ v ≤*wf w)₃, on which we can apply the induction hypothesis
because their size are smaller despite not being in the same index.
Suppose we are now in the case 1, that is (Γ ⊢ u wf)₁, let’s prove (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u wf)₁.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree (Γ ⊢ u wf)₁.
Rule Wf-PrS or rule Wf-PrE with u=x :
In this case, we have x ◁ t∈Γ,
and therefore x ◁ t∈Γ∪Γ′.
By assumption, we have Γ,Γ′;s@s′ prevalid, hence Γ,Γ′ prevalid.
Hence by rule Wf-PrS or rule Wf-PrE, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ x wf.
Rule Wf-Top:
In this case, we have as premises Γ prevalid.
By assumption, we have Γ,Γ′;s@s′ prevalid, hence Γ,Γ′ prevalid.
We now have Γ,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ wf by rule Wf-Top.
Rule Wf-Fun with u=λ x ≤ a.b :
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ a wf)₁ and (Γ,x ≤ a ⊢ b wf)₁.
Because x is a fresh variable, we can always alpha convert it to another name that does not exist already,
and as such the variable x is not used in Γ′ : no annotation of x exist in Γ′,
and all the annotations of Γ′ does not reference x.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ a wf)₁ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u wf)₁,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ a wf)₁.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ,x ≤ a ⊢ b wf)₁ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u wf)₁,
we obtain (Γ,x ≤ a,Γ′ ⊢ b wf)₁.
Because x does not exist in Γ′, we have (Γ,Γ′,x ≤ a ⊢ b wf)₁.
By rule Wf-Fun, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ λ x ≤ a.b wf.
Rule Wf-App with u=a b :
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ x ≤ w.⊤)₃ and (Γ ⊢ b ≤*wf w)₃.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ x ≤ w.⊤)₃ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u wf)₁,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ x ≤ w.⊤)₃.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ b ≤*wf w)₃ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u wf)₁,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ b ≤*wf w)₃.
By rule Wf-App, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ a b wf.
Suppose we are now in the case 2, that is (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂, let’s prove (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂.
Rule Ws-Rfl:
In this case, we have u=v=t.
By using the induction hypothesis on our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ t ≤wf t.
Rule Ws-Lf1:
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ v′◁_wft)₂,
(Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′)_i.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ v′◁_wft)₂ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v′◁_wft)₂.
By using Lemma 22
we obtain Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′
from Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≡ v′.
By rule Ws-Lf1, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v◁_wft.
Rule Ws-Lf2:
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ v′ ≤wf t)₂,
(Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′)_i, (Γ ⊢ v wf)₁ and (Γ ⊢ v′ wf)₁.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ v′ ≤wf t)₂ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v′ ≤wf t)₂.
By using the induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ v wf)₁ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v wf)₁.
By using the induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ v′ wf)₁ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v′ wf)₁.
By using Lemma 21,
we obtain Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′
from Γ;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′.
By rule Ws-Lf2, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v ≤wf t.
Rule Ws-Rgh:
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ v◁_wft′)₂,
(Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′)_i.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ v◁_wft′)₂ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u◁_wfv)₂,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v◁_wft′)₂.
By using Lemma 22, we obtain Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
By rule Ws-Rgh, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ v◁_wft.
Suppose we are now in the case 3, that is (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃, let’s prove (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃.
We distinguish cases based on the last rule used in the derivation tree (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃.
Rule Ws-Sub:
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂.
By using the induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤wf v)₂.
By rule Ws-Sub, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤*wf v.
Rule Ws-Trs:
In this case, we have as premises (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf w)₃ and (Γ ⊢ w ≤*wf v)₃.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf w)₃ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤*wf w)₃.
By induction hypothesis on the subtree (Γ ⊢ w ≤*wf v)₃ of our assumption (Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v)₃,
we obtain (Γ,Γ′ ⊢ w ≤*wf v)₃.
By rule Ws-Trs, we obtain Γ,Γ′ ⊢ u ≤*wf v.

paper: Lemma 21 (Weakening of context - Subtyping reduction).
Let Γ;s and Γ′ be two contexts such that Γ,Γ′;s is prevalid.
Let u and v be terms.
We have the following relations:
If Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v then Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
We distinguish based on the last rule used.
Rule Ms-Pro:
In this case, we have u=x and v=t with x ≤ t∈Γ.
Because x ≤ t∈Γ, we have x ≤ t∈Γ∪Γ′.
By assumption, we have Γ,Γ′;s@s′ prevalid, hence Γ,Γ′;s prevalid.
Hence by rule Ms-Pro, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ x ⟶≤ t.
Rule Ms-Top:
In this case, we have Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ ⊤ and
the derivation has no premises other than the prevalidity of the context.
By assumption, we know that Γ,Γ′;s is prevalid.
Hence, by rule Ms-Top, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ ⊤.
Rule Ms-Equ:
In this case, we have Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v with premise
Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
By Lemma 22, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
Hence, by rule Ms-Equ, we conclude that Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
Rule Ms-App:
In this case, we have u=a b and v=a′ b with premise
By the induction hypothesis, we obtain Γ,Γ′;b::s ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
Hence, by rule Ms-App, we conclude that Γ,Γ′;s ⊢ a b ⟶≤ a′ b.
Rule Ms-FOp:
In this case, u=λ x ≤ t.a, v=λ x ≤ t.a′ and s=α::s₀
with premise Γ,x ≡ α;s₀ ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
By the induction hypothesis we obtain Γ,Γ′,x ≡ α;s₀ ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
From the fact that x is fresh
(hence can be renamed so that it never appears in Γ′ ), we obtain
Γ,Γ′,x ≡ α;s₀ ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
Therefore, by rule Ms-FOp, we deduce that
Γ,Γ′;α::s₀ ⊢ λ x ≤ t.a ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t.a′.
Rule Ms-Fun:
In this case, u=λ x ≤ t.a, v=λ x ≤ t.a′ and s=nil
with premise Γ,x ≤ t;nil ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
By the induction hypothesis we obtain Γ,Γ′,x ≤ t;nil ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
From the fact that x is fresh
(hence can be renamed so that it never appears in Γ′ ), we obtain
Γ,Γ′,x ≤ t;nil ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
Therefore, by rule Ms-Fun, we deduce that
Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t.a ⟶≤ λ x ≤ t.a′.

paper: Lemma 22 (Weakening of context - Equivalence reduction).
Let Γ;s and Γ′;s′ be two extended contexts such that Γ,Γ′;s@s′ is prevalid.
Let u and v be terms.
We have the following relations:
If Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v then Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
We distinguish based on the last rule used.
Rule Me-Var:
In this case, we have u=x and v=x.
By assumption, we have Γ,Γ′;s@s′ prevalid.
Hence by rule Me-Var, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ x ⟶≡ x.
Rule Me-Pro:
In this case, we have u=x and v=α′ with x ≡ α′∈Γ
and Γ;s ⊢ α ⟶≡ α′.
By induction, we have Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ α ⟶≡ α′.
Because x ≡ α∈Γ, we have x ≡ α∈Γ∪Γ′.
By assumption, we have Γ,Γ′;s@s′ prevalid.
Hence by rule Me-Pro, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ x ⟶≡ α′.
Rule Me-App:
In this case, we have u=a b and v=a′ b′ with premises
Γ;b::s ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and Γ;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
By the induction hypothesis, we obtain
Γ,Γ′;b::s@s′ ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and
Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
Hence, by rule Me-App, we conclude that
Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ a b ⟶≡ a′ b′.
Rule Me-Top:
In this case, we have Γ;s ⊢ ⊤ ⟶≡ ⊤ and
the derivation has no premises other than the prevalidity of the context.
By assumption, we know that Γ,Γ′;s@s′ is prevalid.
Hence, by rule Me-Top, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ ⊤ ⟶≡ ⊤.
Rule Me-Fun:
In this case, u=λ x ≤ a.b, v=λ x ≤ a′.b′ and s=nil
with premises Γ;nil ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and
Γ,x ≤ a;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
By the induction hypothesis we obtain
Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and
Γ,x ≤ a,Γ′;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
From the fact that x is fresh
(hence can be renamed so that it never appears in Γ′ ), we obtain
Γ,Γ′,x ≤ a;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
Therefore, by rule Me-Fun, we deduce that
Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ a.b ⟶≡ λ x ≤ a′.b′.
Rule Me-FOp:
In this case, u=λ x ≤ a.b, v=λ x ≤ a′.b′ and s=α::s₀
with premises Γ;nil ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and
Γ;x ≡ α;s₀ ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
By the induction hypothesis we obtain
Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and
Γ,x ≡ α,Γ′;s₀@s′ ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
From the fact that x is fresh
(hence can be renamed so that it never appears in Γ′ ), we obtain
Γ,Γ′,x ≡ α;s₀@s′ ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
Therefore, by rule Me-FOp, we deduce that
Γ,Γ′;α::s₀@s′ ⊢ λ x ≤ a.b ⟶≡ λ x ≤ a′.b′.
Rule Me-Bet:
In this case, u=(λ x ≤ a.b) c and v=b′[x c′]
with premises Γ;s ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′ and
Γ;nil ⊢ c ⟶≡ c′.
By the induction hypothesis we obtain
Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′ and
Γ,Γ′;nil ⊢ c ⟶≡ c′.
Therefore, by rule Me-Bet, we deduce that
Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ (λ x ≤ a.b) c ⟶≡ b′[x c′].
Rule Me-TAp:
In this case, u=⊤ b and v=⊤ with premise Γ;s prevalid.
By assumption, we know that Γ,Γ′;s@s′ is prevalid.
Hence, by rule Me-TAp, we obtain Γ,Γ′;s@s′ ⊢ ⊤ b ⟶≡ ⊤.

paper: Lemma 23 (Narrowing of context in well-formedness derivation).
Let Γ and Γ′ be two contexts.
Let t, t′, and u be terms.
If Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u wf and Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′ and Γ ⊢ t′ wf,
then Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ u wf.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ u wf.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used in the derivation tree.
Rule Wf-PrS or rule Wf-PrE with u=y :
By assumption, we have y ◁ t_y∈Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ for some t_y,
and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ prevalid.
By Lemma 26, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ prevalid.
Either this subtype annotation is x ≤ t, or it’s another one.
In the former case, we have y=x,
and x ≤ t′∈Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′, hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ u wf
by rule Wf-PrS.
In the latter case, we have y ◁ t_y∈Γ∪Γ′,
hence y ◁ t_y∈Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′
hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ u wf by rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE.
Rule Wf-Top:
By assumption, u=⊤ and
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ prevalid.
By Lemma 26, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ prevalid.
Hence, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ wf by rule Wf-Top.
Rule Wf-Fun with u=λ y ≤ v.w :
We have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ λ y ≤ v.w wf with premise
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,y ≤ v ⊢ w wf.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′,y ≤ v ⊢ w wf.
Hence, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ λ y ≤ v.w wf by Wf-Fun.
Rule Wf-App with u=a b :
By assumption, there exist some term z such that
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ z.⊤ and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ b ≤*wf z.
We prove the case Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ z.⊤, the other one is done by the exact same reasoning.
We wish to prove Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ z.⊤
We first decompose Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ z.⊤
into Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤wf a₀ ≤wf·s ≤wf a_n ≤wf λ y ≤ z.⊤,
to then prove we can transform each of these step of this derivation
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ b ≤wf c into
Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ b ≤*wf c.
To do so, we do the same reasoning as in Lemma 7 by using instead Lemmas
Hence by using the rule Ws-Trs, we later obtain Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ z.⊤.
By using the same reasoning on Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ b ≤*wf z,
we obtain Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ b ≤*wf z.
Hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a b wf by rule Wf-App.

paper: Lemma 24 (Narrowing of context in subtyping reductions).
Let Γ;s be an extended context, let Γ′ be an additional context.
Let u, v, t and t′ be terms.
If Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v and Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
Assume that both u, v are well-formed in context Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′.
Assume also Γ ⊢ t′ wf.
Then there exists a term v′ such that we have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v′,
and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ v ⟶≤ v′,
and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ v′ wf.
Proof.
If the derivation Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v
does not make a promotion of x to t, then we have
Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v
and v′=v satisfy the lemma.
Else, if the derivation Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤ v
make a promotion of x to t, then we have
Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[x]⟶≤ Co[t′] with
Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[t′]⟶≡ Co[t]
by weakening to adapt the context and obtain the last derivation from Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
We now need to show that v′ is well-formed in context Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′
by induction on the structure of v′.
Case v′=x :
A variable is well-formed by rule Wf-PrS or Wf-PrE.
Case v′=⊤ :
We have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ wf by rule Wf-Top.
Case v′=λ y ≤ t″.w :
We have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ λ y ≤ t″.w wf
by rule Wf-Fun with premise Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′,y ≤ t″ ⊢ w wf.
By the induction hypothesis, we have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′,y ≤ t″ ⊢ w wf.
Case v′=a b :
Because v′ and u are the same term, except for a promotion of x to t in head position,
we know in our induction that u=a′ b′ with b′=b.
Because u is well-formed, we have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a′ ≤*wf λ y ≤ w.⊤
and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ b′ ≤*wf w.
We now prove Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ w.⊤,
which will allow us to conclude that v′ is well-formed by rule Wf-App.
We have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a′ ≤*wf λ y ≤ w.⊤.
By using the induction hypothesis on a, we know that it’s well-formed in context Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′.
Because a′ is a but with a promotion of x to t in head position, we have
Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤wf a′ from rule Ws-Lf2.
Hence we can conclude that Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a ≤*wf λ y ≤ w.⊤.

paper: Lemma 25 (Narrowing of context in equivalence reductions).
Let Γ;s be an extended context, let Γ′ be an additional context.
Let u, v, t and t′ be terms.
If Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v and Γ;nil ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
Then we have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
Proof.
We do an induction on the derivation tree of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used.
Rule Me-Var:
We have u=v=y some variable.
The derivation Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v hence holds by rule Me-Var.
Rule Me-Pro:
We have u=y and v=α′ with y ≡ α∈Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ α ⟶≡ α′.
By prevalidity of the context, we know that y≠ x, and as a result we have y ≡ α∈Γ,Γ′,
hence y ≡ α∈Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′.
By rule Me-Pro, we therefore have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ y ⟶≡ α′.
Rule Me-Top:
By assumption, we have
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ ⟶≡ ⊤ with premise
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ prevalid.
By Lemma 26, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;s prevalid.
By rule Ms-Top, we have Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;s ⊢ ⊤ ⟶≡ ⊤.
Rule Me-App:
We have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ a b ⟶≡ a′ b′ with premises Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;b::s ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;b::s ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
Hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ a b ⟶≡ a′ b′ by Ms-App.
Rule Me-Fun:
We have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ λ y ≤ w.u ⟶≡ λ y ≤ w′.u′
with Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,y ≤ w;nil ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′ and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ w ⟶≡ w′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′,y ≤ w;nil ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′
and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ w ⟶≡ w′.
Thus, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ λ y ≤ w.u ⟶≡ λ y ≤ w′.u′ by Me-Fun.
Rule Me-FOp:
We have
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;α::s ⊢ λ y ≤ w.u ⟶≡ λ y ≤ w′.u′
with premise Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,y ≡ α;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′ and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ w ⟶≡ w′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′,y ≡ α;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′ and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ w ⟶≡ w′.
Hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ λ y ≤ w.u ⟶≡ λ y ≤ w′.u′ by Me-FOp.
Rule Me-Bet:
We have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ (λ y ≤ a.b) c ⟶≡ b′[y c′] with premises
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′ and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ c ⟶≡ c′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;s ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′ and Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;nil ⊢ c ⟶≡ c′.
Hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ (λ y ≤ a.b) c ⟶≡ b′[y c′] by Me-Bet.
Rule Me-TAp:
We have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ ⊤ b ⟶≡ ⊤ with premise Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s prevalid.
By Lemma 26, Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′;s prevalid.
Hence Γ,x ≤ t′,Γ′ ⊢ ⊤ b ⟶≡ ⊤ by Me-TAp.

paper: Lemma 26 (Narrowing prevalidity).
Let Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′s be an extended prevalid context,
and t′ such that Γ;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
Then Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′;s is prevalid.
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′s prevalid.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used.
Rule Pv-Emp:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′=ε.
Hence Γ=ε and Γ′=ε.
By assumption, we have Γ;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
We need to prove that Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′;s is prevalid,
which is equivalent to proving that x ◁ t′;s is prevalid.
Because Γ=ε, we have fv(t′)=.
Hence x ◁ t′;s is prevalid.
Rule Pv-Ctx:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′=Γ₀,y ≤ t_y
with Γ₀ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₀) and fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₀).
Either y ≤ t_y is x ◁ t, or it is in Γ₀ or Γ′.
If y ≤ t_y is x ◁ t, then Γ₀=Γ and Γ′=ε.
By assumption, we have Γ;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
We need to prove that Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′;s is prevalid,
which is equivalent to proving that Γ,x ◁ t′;s is prevalid.
Because Γ₀=Γ, we have Γ prevalid.
Because x∉dom(Γ), we have x∉dom(Γ).
Because fv(t)⊆dom(Γ) and Γ;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′,
we have fv(t′)⊆dom(Γ).
Hence Γ,x ◁ t′;s is prevalid.
If y ≤ t_y is in Γ₀, then Γ₀=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y and Γ′=ε.
By induction hypothesis, Γ₁,x ◁ t′,Γ′;s is prevalid.
Hence Γ₁,x ◁ t′,Γ′,y ≤ t_y;s is prevalid.
If y ≤ t_y is in Γ′, then Γ′=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ and Γ′=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y.
By induction hypothesis, Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ₁;s is prevalid.
Hence Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ₁,y ≤ t_y;s is prevalid.
Rule Pv-EqA:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′=Γ₀,y ≡ α
with Γ₀ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₀) and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₀).
Either y ≡ α is x ◁ t, or it is in Γ₀ or Γ′.
If y ≡ α is x ◁ t, then Γ₀=Γ and Γ′=ε.
By assumption, we have Γ;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′.
We need to prove that Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′;s is prevalid,
which is equivalent to proving that Γ,x ◁ t′;s is prevalid.
Because Γ₀=Γ, we have Γ prevalid.
Because x∉dom(Γ), we have x∉dom(Γ).
Because fv(t)⊆dom(Γ) and Γ;s ⊢ t ⟶≡ t′,
we have fv(t′)⊆dom(Γ).
Hence Γ,x ◁ t′;s is prevalid.
If y ≡ α is in Γ₀, then Γ₀=Γ₁,y ≡ α for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ₁,y ≡ α and Γ′=ε.
By induction hypothesis, Γ₁,x ◁ t′,Γ′;s is prevalid.
Hence Γ₁,x ◁ t′,Γ′,y ≡ α;s is prevalid.
If y ≡ α is in Γ′, then Γ′=Γ₁,y ≡ α for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ and Γ′=Γ₁,y ≡ α.
By induction hypothesis, Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ₁;s is prevalid.
Hence Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ₁,y ≡ α;s is prevalid.
Rule Pv-Nil:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s=Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;nil
with Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′ prevalid.
By induction hypothesis, Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′ prevalid.
Hence Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′;nil is prevalid.
Rule Pv-Sta:
In this case, we have
Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s=Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;α::s₀
with Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s₀ prevalid and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′).

Hence Γ,x ◁ t′,Γ′;α::s₀ is prevalid.

paper: Proposition 27 (Reduction preserves subtyping derivation).
Let Γ;s be an extended context.
Let u, u′ and v be terms such that
Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v and
u ↦ u′, and
Γ ⊢ u′ wf.
Then Γ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf v.
Proof.
By 17, we have Γ;nil ⊢ u ⟶≡ u′.
By rule Ws-Rfl and Ws-Lf1, we have Γ ⊢ u′ ≤wf u.
From Proposition 12, we have Γ ⊢ u wf
from Γ ⊢ u ≤*wf v.
Hence rule Ws-Sub, we have Γ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf u.
By Ws-Trs, we then have Γ ⊢ u′ ≤*wf v.

        → ∀ {Γ u u' v}
        → Γ ⊢ u ⊑*wf[ sub-m ] v
        → u ↦ u'
        → Γ ⊢ u' wf
        → Γ ⊢ u' ⊑*wf[ sub-m ] v
27.account: Ws-Rfl gives u′ ⊑wf u′; Ws-Rgh walks the right-hand side back along u ⟶≡ u′; Ws-Sub lifts that to the transitive closure and Ws-Trs composes. Isolated as push≡*wf, which works for any equivalence step in either mode.

paper: Lemma 28 (Substitution preserves prevalidity).
Let Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s be an extended context.
If Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s is prevalid, then Γ,Γ′[x t];s[x t] is prevalid.
If Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′ is prevalid, then Γ,Γ′[x t] is prevalid.
Proof.
We prove the first result, the second is similar.
We now do an induction on the derivation tree Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s prevalid.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used in the derivation tree of Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s prevalid.
Rule Pv-Emp:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′=ε.
Hence Γ=ε and Γ′=ε.
The result to prove in this case is Γ,Γ′[x t]=ε is prevalid,
which holds by rule Pv-Emp.
Rule Pv-Ctx:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′=Γ₀,y ≤ t_y
with Γ₀ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₀) and fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₀).
Either y ≤ t_y is x ◁ t, or it is in Γ₀ or Γ′.
If y ≤ t_y is x ◁ t, then Γ₀=Γ and Γ′=ε.
We need to prove that Γ,Γ′[x t]=Γ is prevalid,
which holds by assumption.
If y ≤ t_y is in Γ₀, then Γ₀=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y and Γ′=ε.
By induction hypothesis, Γ₁,Γ′[x t]=Γ₁ is prevalid.
Because y∉dom(Γ₁), we have y∉dom(Γ₁,Γ′[x t]).
Because fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₁), we have fv(t_y[x t])⊆dom(Γ₁,Γ′[x t]).
Hence Γ₁,Γ′[x t],y ≤ t_y[x t] is prevalid.
If y ≤ t_y is in Γ′, then Γ′=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ and Γ′=Γ₁,y ≤ t_y.
By induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ₁[x t] is prevalid.
Because y∉dom(Γ₁), we have y∉dom(Γ,Γ₁[x t]).
Because fv(t_y)⊆dom(Γ₁), we have fv(t_y[x t])⊆dom(Γ,Γ₁[x t]).
Hence Γ,Γ₁[x t],y ≤ t_y[x t] is prevalid.
Rule Pv-EqA:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′=Γ₀,y ≡ α
with Γ₀ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₀) and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₀).
Either y ≡ α is x ◁ t, or it is in Γ₀ or Γ′.
If y ≡ α is x ◁ t, then Γ₀=Γ and Γ′=ε.
We need to prove that Γ,Γ′[x t]=Γ is prevalid,
which holds by assumption.
If y ≡ α is in Γ₀, then Γ₀=Γ₁,y ≡ α for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ₁,y ≡ α and Γ′=ε.
By induction hypothesis, Γ₁,Γ′[x t]=Γ₁ is prevalid.
Because y∉dom(Γ₁), we have y∉dom(Γ₁,Γ′[x t]).
Because fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₁), we have fv(α[x t])⊆dom(Γ₁,Γ′[x t]).
Hence Γ₁,Γ′[x t],y ≡ α[x t] is prevalid.
If y ≡ α is in Γ′, then Γ′=Γ₁,y ≡ α for some Γ₁.
We have Γ₁ prevalid and y∉dom(Γ₁) and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₁).
We also have Γ=Γ and Γ′=Γ₁,y ≡ α.
By induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ₁[x t] is prevalid.
Because y∉dom(Γ₁), we have y∉dom(Γ,Γ₁[x t]).
Because fv(α)⊆dom(Γ₁), we have fv(α[x t])⊆dom(Γ,Γ₁[x t]).
Hence Γ,Γ₁[x t],y ≡ α[x t] is prevalid.
Rule Pv-Nil:
In this case, we have Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s=Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;nil
with Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′ prevalid.
By induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ′[x t] prevalid.
Hence Γ,Γ′[x t];nil is prevalid.
Rule Pv-Sta:
In this case, we have
Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s=Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;α::s₀
with Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′;s₀ prevalid and fv(α)⊆dom(Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′).
By induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ′[x t];s₀[x t] prevalid.
Because fv(α)⊆dom(Γ,x ◁ t,Γ′),
we have fv(α[x t])⊆dom(Γ,Γ′[x t]).
Hence Γ,Γ′[x t];α[x t]::s₀[x t] is prevalid.

paper: Lemma 29 (Promotion under substitution outside of covariant contexts).
Let Γ;s be an extended context, and Γ′ be a logical context,
such that Γ,Γ′[x\α];nil is prevalid.
Let t and α be terms.
Let Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[x]⟶≤ Co[t] be a derivation
for some covariant context Co.
Then Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ Co_[x\α][x]⟶≤ Co_[x\α][t].
Proof.
By induction on u. We distinguish cases based on the structure of u.
Impossible by assumption.
u=x :
Nothing to do.
u=λ y ≤ z.u′ :
By assumption, we have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[λ y ≤ z.u′]⟶≤ Co[λ y ≤ z.v].
Let P′ be such that Co[λ y ≤ z.u′]=Co′[u′].
Our derivation is now Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co′[u′]⟶≤ Co′[v].
By induction, we have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ Co′_[x\α][u′]⟶≤ Co′_[x\α][v].
By definition of Co′, this is
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ Co_[x\α][λ y ≤ z.u′[x\α]]⟶≤ Co_[x\α][λ y ≤ z.v[x\α]].
To conclude we need to prove that
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ Co_[x\α][λ y ≤ z[x\α].u′[x\α]]⟶≤ Co_[x\α][λ y ≤ z[x\α].v[x\α]]
holds.
Because this derivation make a promotion of x to t, it doesn’t do a promotion of y to its type annotation,
as a result this derivation holds.
By alpha conversion, the term λ y ≤ z[x\α].u′[x\α]
is equal to (λ y ≤ z.u′)[x\α], and similarly for λ y ≤ z[x\α].v[x\α].
Hence the result.
u=u′ u″ :
By assumption, we have
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co[u′ u″]⟶≤ Co[v′ v″].
Let P′ be such that Co[u′ u″]=Co′[u′].
Our derivation is now Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ Co′[](u′) ⟶≤ Co′[](v′).
By induction, we have Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ (Co′[])[x\α](u′) ⟶≤ (Co′[])[x\α](v′).
By definition of P′, this is Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ Co_[x\α][u′ u″[x\α]]⟶≤ Co_[x\α][v′ v″[x\α]].
To conclude we need to prove that
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ Co_[x\α][u′[x\α] u″[x\α]]⟶≤ Co_[x\α][v′[x\α] v″[x\α]]
holds.
Because this derivation make a promotion of x to t, it doesn’t use the annotation of u″ in the stack,
as a result this derivation holds.
By definition of the substitution, the term u′[x\α] u″[x\α]
is equal to (u′ u″)[x\α], and similarly for v′[x\α] v″[x\α],
hence the result.

paper: Lemma 30 (Promotion under substitution inside of covariant contexts).
Let Γ;s be an extended context.
Let Γ′ be a logical context,
such that Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α] is prevalid.
Let u, v, t and α be terms.
Let x be a variable.
If Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v,
such that this derivation is NOT of the form Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ Co[x]⟶≤ Co[t]
for some covariant context P.
Then we have Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]⟶≤ v[x\α].
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≤ v.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used.
Rule Ms-Pro:
In this case, we have u=y and v=t_y with y ≤ t_y∈Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′
and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ prevalid.
We know that y≠x from the assumption that our derivation does not make a promotion of x to t.
If y ≤ t_y∈Γ, by prevalidity of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ we know
there is no instance of x in t_y, and as such we have t_y[x\α]=t_y.
Now we have Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ y ⟶≤ t_y
by rule Ms-Pro, which is the desired result.
If y ≤ t_y∈Γ′, we have by definition of the substitution on context,
y ≤ t_y[x\α]∈Γ′[x\α],
and as a result we have Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ y ⟶≤ t_y[x\α]
by rule Ms-Pro.
Rule Ms-Top:
In this case, we have
u=y and v=⊤.
We need to show Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]⟶≤ ⊤[x\α].
Since ⊤[x\α]=⊤,
we need to show Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]⟶≤ ⊤,
which holds by rule Ms-Top.
Rule Ms-Equ:
In this case, we have
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
By Lemma 31, Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]⟶≡ v[x\α].
Hence, Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]⟶≤ v[x\α] by Ms-Equ.
Rule Ms-App:
In this case, we have u=a b and v=a′ b with premise Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;b::s ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ′[x\α];b[x\α]::s[x\α]⊢ a[x\α]⟶≤ a′[x\α].
Hence Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ a[x\α] b[x\α]⟶≤ a′[x\α] b[x\α] by Ms-App,
which is by definition of the substitution,
equivalent to Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ (a b)[x\α]⟶≤ (a′ b)[x\α].
Rule Ms-Fun:
In this case, u=λ y ≤ w.a, v=λ y ≤ w.a′ with
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,y ≤ w;nil ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ′[x\α],y ≤ w[x\α];nil ⊢ a[x\α]⟶≤ a′[x\α].
Thus, Γ,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ λ y ≤ w[x\α].a[x\α]⟶≤ λ y ≤ w[x\α].a′[x\α] by Ms-Fun,
which is by definition of the substitution, and because by alpha conversion we have y≠x,
equivalent to Γ,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ (λ y ≤ w.a)[x\α]⟶≤ (λ y ≤ w.a′)[x\α].
Rule Ms-FOp:
In this case, u=λ y ≤ w.a, v=λ y ≤ w.a′ with Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,y ≡ β;s ⊢ a ⟶≤ a′.
By the induction hypothesis, Γ,Γ′[x\α],y ≡ β[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ a[x\α]⟶≤ a′[x\α].
Thus, Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ λ y ≤ w[x\α].a[x\α]⟶≤ λ y ≤ w[x\α].a′[x\α] by Ms-FOp,
which is by definition of the substitution, and because by alpha conversion we have y≠x,
equivalent to Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ (λ y ≤ w.a)[x\α]⟶≤ (λ y ≤ w.a′)[x\α].
30.sig:
⟶ˢ-drop′ : ∀ (Δ : Ctx) {Γ x t α s u v}
         → LC α → fv α ⊑ dom Γ
         → ¬ CoPair x t u v
         → (Δ ++ (x , sub , t) ∷ Γ) ∣ s ⊢ u ⟶ˢ v
         → (substCtx x α Δ ++ Γ) ∣ (substStack x α s) ⊢ (u [ x := α ]) ⟶ˢ (v [ x := α ])
30.account: The side condition is moved from the derivation to the term. Every promotion derivation runs down a covariant spine to its leaf, since the structural rules are exactly Ms-App into an operator and Ms-Fun/Ms-FOp into a body, so a term with no covariant spine ending at x admits no derivation promoting it. That matters because a condition on a derivation cannot be carried into a cofinite family, where different witnesses could take different rules.

paper: Lemma 31 (Reduction under substitution).
Let Γ;s be an extended context.
Let Γ′ be a logical context,
such that Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α] is prevalid.
Let u, v, t and α be terms.
Let x be a variable.
If Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v,
then Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ u[x\α]⟶≡ v[x\α].
Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used.
Rule Me-Var:
In this case, we have u=y and v=y with Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ prevalid.
If y=x, then u[x\α]=α and v[x\α]=α.
We need to show Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ α ⟶≡ α,
which holds by reflexivity (Proposition 18).
If y≠ x, then u[x\α]=y and v[x\α]=y.
We need to show Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ y ⟶≡ y,
which holds by rule Me-Var.
Rule Me-Pro:
In this case, we have u=y and v=α″
with y ≡ α′∈Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′,
and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ ⊢ α′ ⟶≡ α″,
and Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ prevalid.
Because Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ is prevalid, there is a single annotation of x,
and because it’s x ≤ t it cannot be y ≡ α′ and as such we have y≠x.
If y ≡ α′∈Γ, by prevalidity of Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′ we know
there is no instance of x in α″, and as such we have α″[x\α]=α′ and
y ≡ α′∈Γ,Γ′[x\α].
Now we have Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ y ⟶≡ α″
by rule Me-Pro, which is the desired result.
If y ≡ α′∈Γ′, we have by definition of the substitution on context,
hence y ≡ α′[x\α]∈Γ,Γ′[x\α].
By induction, we have Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ α′[x\α]⟶≡ α″[x\α],
hence by rule Me-Pro, we have Γ,Γ′[x\α];s[x\α]⊢ y ⟶≡ α″[x\α].
Rule Me-App:
In this case, we have u=a b and
v=a′ b′ with premises
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;b::s ⊢ a ⟶≡ a′ and
Γ,x ≤ t,Γ′;nil ⊢ b ⟶≡ b′.
By the induction hypothesis, we obtain
Γ,Γ′[x\α];b[x\α]::s[x\α]⊢ a[x\α]⟶≡ a′[x\α] and
Γ,Γ′[x\α];nil ⊢ b[x\α]⟶≡ b′[x\α].
Hence, by rule Me-App, we conclude that

paper: Lemma 32 (Reduction under substitution - auxiliary for the commutation theorem).
Let Γ;s be an extended context.
Let u, u′, v and v′ be terms.

Proof.
By induction on the derivation tree of Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′;s ⊢ u ⟶≡ v.
We distinguish cases on the last rule used.
Rule Me-Var:
In this case, we have u=y and v=y with Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′ prevalid.
If y=x, then u[x v]=v and v[x v]=v.
We need to show Γ,Γ′[x v];s[x v]⊢ v ⟶≡ v,
which holds by reflexivity (Proposition 18).
If y≠ x, then u[x v]=y and v[x v]=y.
We need to show Γ,Γ′[x v];s[x v]⊢ y ⟶≡ y,
which holds by rule Me-Var.
Rule Me-Pro with u=y≠ x :
In this case, we have u=y and v=α″
with y ≡ α′∈Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′,
and Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′ ⊢ α′ ⟶≡ α″,
and Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′ prevalid.
If y ≡ α′∈Γ, by prevalidity of Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′ we know
there is no instance of x in α″, and as such we have α″[x v]=α′ and
y ≡ α′∈Γ,Γ′[x v].
Now we have Γ,Γ′[x v];s[x v]⊢ y ⟶≡ α″
by rule Me-Pro, which is the desired result.
If y ≡ α′∈Γ′, we have by definition of the substitution on context,
y ≡ α′[x v]∈Γ′[x v],
hence y ≡ α′[x v]∈Γ,Γ′[x v].
By induction, we have Γ,Γ′[x v];s[x v]⊢ α′[x v]⟶≡ α″[x v],
hence by rule Me-Pro, we have Γ,Γ′[x v];s[x v]⊢ y ⟶≡ α″[x v].

In this case, we have u=x and v=α with premise Γ,x ≡ v,Γ′;s ⊢ v ⟶≡ α.

Therefore induction we have Γ,Γ′[x v];s[x v]⊢ v ⟶≡ α.

In this case, we have u=a b and

paper: Lemma 33 (Congruence of ≤ ).
Let Γ;s be an extended context, and let u, u′, v, t and α be terms
We have these six congruence relations:
If Γ;v::s ⊢ u ≤ u′, then Γ;s ⊢ u v ≤ u′ v.
If Γ;v::s ⊢ u ≤* u′, then Γ;s ⊢ u v ≤* u′ v.
If Γ,x ≤ t;nil ⊢ u ≤ u′ then Γ;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ≤ λ x ≤ t.u′.
If Γ,x ≤ t;nil ⊢ u ≤* u′ then Γ;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ≤* λ x ≤ t.u′.
If Γ,x ≡ α;s ⊢ u ≤ u′ then Γ;α::s ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ≤ λ x ≤ t.u′.
If Γ,x ≡ α;s ⊢ u ≤* u′ then Γ;α::s ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ≤* λ x ≤ t.u′.
Proof.
We do the first case. Every other case is similar:
it lifts Lemmas 34 and 35.
Suppose we have Γ;v::s ⊢ u ≤ u′.
By definition of the subtype relation, we have a term t such that
Γ;v::s ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ t and Γ;v::s ⊢ u′ ⟶≤↠ t.
By Lemma 35, we have Γ;s ⊢ u v ⟶≡↠ t v
from Γ;v::s ⊢ u ⟶≡↠ t.
By Lemma 34, we have Γ;s ⊢ u′ v ⟶≤↠ t v
from Γ;v::s ⊢ u′ ⟶≤↠ t.
We then conclude by definition of the subtype relation with the intermediate term t v.

paper: Lemma 34 (Congruence of ⟶≤ ).
Let Γ;s be an extended context, and let u, u′, v and t be terms
We have these congruence relations:
If Γ;v::s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ u′, then Γ;s ⊢ u v ⟶≤↠ u′ v.
If Γ,x ≤ t;nil ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ u′ then Γ;nil ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ⟶≤↠ λ x ≤ t.u′.
If Γ,x ≡ α;s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ u′ then Γ;α::s ⊢ λ x ≤ t.u ⟶≤↠ λ x ≤ t.u′.
Proof.
For the first case, take Γ;v::s ⊢ u ⟶≤↠ u′.
On each Γ;v::s ⊢ a ⟶≤ b subderivation of our initial multi-step derivation,
we apply the rule Ms-App, to obtain Γ;s ⊢ a v ⟶≤ b v.
By doing so on each subderivation, we finally obtain the derivation Γ;s ⊢ u v ⟶≤↠ u′ v,
which is the desired result.
The other cases are similar, with the use of rules Ms-Fun and Ms-FOp instead.
